parts.title: A Garden Begins
parts.text: Rosa convinced the neighborhood to turn a trash-filled lot into a community garden. At first the soil was dry, and the few seedlings looked **sparse** in the long beds. Tariq, who was **thrifty**, collected scrap wood and old buckets instead of buying supplies. He built a **trellis** from boards and string so the bean vines could climb. Hannah's job was to **nurture** every tiny seedling with water, sunlight, and patience.

parts.title: Midsummer Work
parts.text: By midsummer, bees buzzed through the garden to **pollinate** the squash flowers, and the plants began to **sprawl** across the paths in every direction. Rosa showed the group how to **prune** extra branches so the tomatoes would grow bigger fruit instead of more leaves. But one plot, belonging to a family that had traveled for weeks, suffered from **neglect**; weeds crowded it, and nobody watered it.

parts.title: The Harvest
parts.text: Soon a spotted **blight** crept from that plot toward the rest of the garden. Leaves began to **wither**, curling brown at the edges. Tariq and Hannah pulled the sick plants and bagged them, and Rosa organized neighbors to check every bed daily. The effort worked, and weeks later the surviving plants gave a **bountiful** crop. Neighbors gathered to **reap** baskets of tomatoes, beans, and squash.

parts.title: Growing Together
parts.text: That evening, the whole block shared a picnic dinner made from the garden's vegetables. Rosa noticed that the garden had grown a community along with the plants. Even the family who had been away planted new seeds in the cleared plot, promising to ask for help next time they traveled.

definitions.meaning1: To care for and help something grow and develop. Example: Gardeners nurture tiny seedlings with water and sunlight.
definitions.meaning2: To help an idea or feeling grow. Example: Good teachers nurture a love of reading in their students.

definitions.meaning1: Plentiful; producing or giving a large amount. Example: Farmers celebrated a bountiful harvest of corn and pumpkins.

definitions.meaning1: To trim branches or stems from a plant to help it grow better. Example: In late winter, the gardener will prune the rose bushes.
definitions.meaning2: To cut down by removing parts that are not needed. Example: The editor asked me to prune my story and cut every unnecessary sentence.

definitions.meaning1: A plant disease that causes leaves and stems to wither and die. Example: A fast-spreading blight turned the potato leaves black.
definitions.meaning2: Something that spoils or harms. Example: The abandoned factory was a blight on the neighborhood.

definitions.meaning1: A frame of crossing wood or wire that supports climbing plants. Example: The sweet-pea vines climbed up the wooden trellis beside the fence.

definitions.meaning1: To carry pollen from one flower to another so that seeds and fruit can form. Example: Honeybees pollinate flowers as they carry pollen from bloom to bloom.

definitions.meaning1: To spread out in a wide, untidy way. Example: The vines will sprawl across the whole yard if no one trims them.
definitions.meaning2: To sit or lie with arms and legs stretched out carelessly. Example: After the long hike, he let himself sprawl on the couch.

definitions.meaning1: To dry up, shrink, and lose freshness. Example: Without water, the flowers will wither and turn brown.
definitions.meaning2: To fade away or weaken. Example: His confidence began to wither under the harsh criticism.

definitions.meaning1: To fail to take care of something. Example: If you neglect your plants, they will not survive the summer.
definitions.meaning2: The state of being uncared for. Example: The old house fell into neglect after the owners moved away.
definitions.studentChallenge: If you ___ the lawn all summer, it will turn into a weed patch.

definitions.meaning1: To cut and gather a crop. Example: Farmers reap the wheat when the stalks turn golden.
definitions.meaning2: To receive as a result of effort. Example: Students who practice daily reap the rewards at the recital.

definitions.meaning1: Careful about spending money and using things wisely. Example: Her thrifty habits helped her save money for college.
